topic: Equations of Horizontal and Vertical Lines

lessonData.topic: Equations of Horizontal and Vertical Lines
lessonData.subject: Mathematics / Geometry
lessonData.tagline: Mastering lines that never tilt: why zero slope is flat ground, but sheer cliffs break the math.
lessonData.overview: Horizontal lines maintain a constant y-value and have a gradient of zero, representing perfectly flat paths across the Cartesian plane. In contrast, vertical lines fix a constant x-value and possess an undefined gradient because dividing by a zero change in x is mathematically impossible.

chalkNotes.title: Horizontal & Vertical Lines
chalkNotes.subtitle: Constant Values, Slope Calculation, and Function Rules
chalkNotes.coreRuleOrFormula: Horizontal Line: y = c (Gradient m = 0) | Vertical Line: x = a (Gradient is Undefined)
bulletPoints: Horizontal lines (y = c): Every point has the same y-value. Rise is 0, so m = 0 / run = 0. Parallel to the x-axis.
Vertical lines (x = a): Every point has the same x-value. Run is 0, so m = rise / 0, which is undefined.
Common Misconception Alert: A line parallel to the x-axis is y = c, NOT x = c. Name the line by the coordinate that does NOT change.
Function Test: Vertical lines fail the vertical line test because a single x-value produces infinitely many y-values, so x = a is not a linear function.
keyTakeaways: A gradient of 0 means zero tilt (flat horizontal floor); an undefined gradient means sheer vertical cliff (division by zero).
To write the equation of any horizontal or vertical line, identify which coordinate remains identical for every point on the line.

quiz.question: A straight line passes through the points (-5, 8) and (-5, -3). Which statement correctly identifies its equation, its gradient, and its orientation relative to the coordinate axes?
options: Equation: x = -5 | Gradient: undefined | Parallel to the y-axis
Equation: y = -5 | Gradient: 0 | Parallel to the x-axis
Equation: x = -5 | Gradient: 0 | Parallel to the y-axis
Equation: y = -5 | Gradient: undefined | Parallel to the x-axis
quiz.explanation: Both points share the identical x-coordinate of -5 while the y-coordinates differ, meaning the line is vertical and its equation is x = -5. When calculating the gradient m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) = (-3 - 8) / (-5 - (-5)) = -11 / 0. Division by zero is undefined, so the gradient is undefined. Vertical lines run straight up and down, making this line parallel to the y-axis.
